accuracy.evidence: Facts checked: snow is ice crystals with six-fold (hexagonal) symmetry (Libbrecht, Caltech snowcrystals.com; Met Office 'How snow forms'); ice density about 0.917 g/cm³ against fresh water 1.000 and sea water about 1.025, so floating ice sits with roughly 89–92% under the surface (NOAA Ocean Service 'How much of an iceberg is below the water?'; USGS Water Science School). Icebergs are fresh-water ice calved from glaciers and ice sheets. The adult text avoids the wrong 'air bubbles make ice float' explanation. Lane geometry was checked so each ship round has exactly one clear lane.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented early-years ideas about water and ice (Russell & Watt, SPACE project report 'Evaporation and condensation'; Driver et al. 1994 Making Sense of Secondary Science, ch. on states of matter): snow and ice are not water (sort cards, Ali, m5, tags powder/cloud/glass), big ice sinks because it is heavy (step 3 predict, Dev, p3, tag sink), floating ice sits on top, dry (decoy 'It floats on top, all dry', Fay, tag dry), only the visible tip matters (step 4 predict 'A tiny bit', ship lanes, tag tip), and melted snow vanishes (Hana).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (under 30% similar to every flagship lab). 366 Melting and freezing (flagmelt) covers warming and cooling, 204 Floating and sinking (flagfloat) covers big-versus-small objects in general, and 550 Where water is found (flagwater) sorts salty and fresh water; none asks the learner to identify a six-armed snow crystal, to see that floating ice sits nine tenths under the water line, or to steer ships around the hidden spread of an iceberg.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners discover the six-arm rule by elimination (wrong picks reveal the arm count), see both a small and a big ice block float low while the pebble and coin sink, and must read the hidden underwater outline to choose a lane: the tempting lanes beside the tip crunch, so 'most of it is hidden' is experienced before it is stated. The sort and the children's statements then fix 'snow and ice are frozen water'.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options the task disproves: 'White powder' for snow, 'No, it is rock' for an iceberg, 'It sinks, it is big' for a big ice block, and 'A tiny bit' for how much iceberg is under water. The done message reports the learner's prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with tagged wrong answers and named slips: powder and cloud (snow is ice crystals), arms (count again: six), sink (ice is lighter than the same amount of water), dry (ice floats low), tip (most of an iceberg is hidden), glass (an icicle is frozen water), soft (ice is hard; the hidden part is dangerous). Lab mistakes are named too, e.g. 'That one has 8 arms…' and 'Crunch! The left way hits ice under the water'.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons readability passed (kid under 6.5, adult under 9.5). Kid sentences are short and use the precise words solid, liquid, frozen, crystal, float, sink, tip and iceberg. Canvas text is one short instruction per step, and buttons say exactly what they do (Middle crystal, Solid water (ice), Drop the pebble, Right way, Bea is right).

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases and explanation similarity under 12% to all lessons. Each kid paragraph carries one idea (frozen water is solid; snow is six-armed ice crystals; ice floats low; icebergs are mostly hidden). The adult text gives curriculum links, the science behind six-fold symmetry and flotation, the task order and named slips.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light and dark for every step before, during and after Show me (/workspace/shots/ice-*, ice2-*). Snow crystal cards are about 100 × 125 px, sort bins span the width, tank objects are 40–66 px, statements wrap inside full-width cards. After the first pass the lane buttons were moved to the top of the sky so they no longer cover the iceberg tips, with dashed lane lines showing each ship's path.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all five tasks complete with Show me, challenge shown, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors. Every drag or tap has a button (Left crystal, Liquid water, Drop the ice cube, Middle way, Eli is right), and the canvas aria-label states the current card, what is floating or on the bottom, and which ways have hidden ice after each action.
